channel.title: daryo
channel.description: Regional headlines in English, updated four times a day.

item.title: Ukraine's Funding Deficit May Determine Fate of New EU Budget
item.description: Negotiations for the European Union's next seven-year budget have reached a critical stage, potentially impacting its finalization. The discussions coincide with efforts to address Ukraine's 70 billion euro funding deficit for 2027. The EU is expected to cover about two-thirds of this amount, with other allies providing the rest.

item.title: Taliban Ban Sale of Pakistani Medicines in Kandahar Pharmacies
item.description: The Taliban have prohibited the sale and purchase of Pakistani medicines in Kandahar province, according to local sources. The decision, reportedly ordered by Hibatullah Akhundzada's office, mandates the collection and burning of remaining Pakistani medicine stocks after a specified deadline. Pharmaceutical companies have criticized the ban, citing insufficient domestic production capacity.

item.title: Uzbekistan's Health Ministry Reports on Digital Technology Implementation in Healthcare
item.description: Uzbekistan's Health Ministry is expanding digital technologies in healthcare, with over 20 modules and services implemented. 4,000 medical organizations, 6,000 clinics, and 11,000 pharmacies are now digitized, serving over 38 million citizens. The ministry has procured significant computer and tablet hardware to enhance data processing and storage. AI technologies are being integrated, with plans for wider adoption by 2027.

item.title: Uzbekistan and UAE Deepen Strategic Partnership for Economic Development
item.description: Uzbekistan and the United Arab Emirates are strengthening their strategic partnership, building on mutual trust and mutually beneficial cooperation. Since establishing diplomatic ties in 1992, political dialogue has intensified, alongside significant growth in trade, investment, energy, transport, education, and technology sectors. Bilateral trade reached $1.3 billion in 2025, with $1.2 billion recorded in the first eight months of 2026.

item.title: Uzbekistan Hosts International Seminar on Climate Risks and Green Development
item.description: An international scientific-practical seminar on "The Impact of Water-Climate Risks on Uzbekistan's Economy and Opportunities for Green Development" was held in Tashkent. The event focused on climate resilience, rational water resource use, and the transition to a low-carbon development model. Representatives from Uzbekistan and Russia participated.

item.title: Former Deputy Rinat Zaitov Appointed Head of National Military-Patriotic Center
item.description: Former deputy and poet Rinat Zaitov has been appointed head of the National Military-Patriotic Center of the Armed Forces of Kazakhstan. He stated that Defense Minister Aidoss Myrzakhmetov invited him to the position, expressing a desire to contribute to reforms in the defense sector. Zaitov also mentioned changes to the military oath.

item.title: Turkmenistan Airlines Boosts International Flight Frequency
item.description: Turkmenistan Airlines is increasing the frequency of several international flights starting October 25. Flights to Seoul will double, while services to Milan, Kazan, and Istanbul will see higher frequencies. The airline aims to meet growing demand and integrate into the global transport network.

item.title: Tehran Talks Emphasize Security Cooperation Amid Regional Challenges
item.description: Recent talks in Tehran focused on enhancing security cooperation, particularly concerning Afghanistan's political and security situation. Discussions also touched upon regional economic challenges, including a projected contraction in 2026 and Turkmenistan's gas production targets.

item.title: Afghanistan Ranks 142nd Out of 143 Countries on World Justice Project's Rule of Law Index
item.description: Afghanistan is ranked 142nd out of 143 countries in the World Justice Project's 2026 Rule of Law Index. Denmark, Norway, and Finland lead the index, while Haiti ranks 141st and Venezuela 143rd. The index assesses eight areas, including government power constraints, corruption, and justice systems.

item.title: Roza Aitmatova, Sister of Famous Writer, Dies at 89 in Kyrgyzstan
item.description: Roza Aitmatova, younger sister of writer Chingiz Aitmatov and a witness to Kyrgyz history, has passed away at 89. Born in Moscow in 1937, her family faced hardship after her father's arrest during Stalin's purges. She transformed her family's tragedies into national memory.

item.title: Over 150,000 Kazakhstani Citizens Under Medical Observation After Screenings
item.description: More than 150,000 people in Kazakhstan have been placed under medical observation following screenings conducted in the first nine months of 2026. These individuals will be monitored, undergo follow-up examinations, and receive treatment if necessary. Screenings covered various conditions including glaucoma, diabetes, hypertension, and cancer.

item.title: Taliban Foreign Minister: Drug Trafficking in Afghanistan's Neighborhood is a Major Concern
item.description: The Taliban's acting foreign minister stated that drug cultivation and trafficking in countries neighboring Afghanistan are a significant concern. He emphasized the need for international cooperation to address this issue, highlighting its impact on regional stability and security. The minister did not provide specific details on the scale of the problem or proposed solutions.

item.title: Panjshir Residents Allege Taliban Detentions and Abuse Following Reported Blast
item.description: Residents of Panjshir province's Dara Abdullah Khel district claim Taliban forces detained and beat local elders and religious scholars after a reported explosion. They also allege nighttime movement restrictions and home searches, creating fear. Taliban authorities deny these allegations, with a spokesman stating no arrests were made. The circumstances of the explosion remain unclear.

item.title: 30 Students Studying Abroad Stripped of Scholarships, Says 'El-Yurt Umidi' Foundation Director
item.description: Gulnoza Ismoilova, director of the 'El-Yurt Umidi' foundation, stated that 30 students studying abroad have had their scholarships revoked for various reasons. Some scholarship recipients have not returned to Uzbekistan, while others have experienced a significant decline in their academic performance.

item.title: Police Discover 7 Tons of Waste Illegally Dumped in Turkestan Region Using Drone
item.description: Police in the Turkestan region have identified a case of illegal waste disposal using a drone. A 42-year-old man was found to have dumped approximately 7 tons of household waste in the Sayram district. Administrative measures were taken against the offender, who was also required to clean up the site.

item.title: China Secures Significant Discount on Russian Gas, Underscoring Moscow's Dependence
item.description: China is receiving substantial discounts on Russian natural gas purchases via the Power of Siberia pipeline, paying significantly less than other foreign customers. This pricing reflects Beijing's political support for Russia's war in Ukraine and is crucial for Moscow's funding needs amid Western sanctions. Russia hopes to renegotiate better terms in the future.

item.title: Kazakhstan and US discuss prospects for small modular reactors
item.description: Kazakhstan and the United States have discussed the potential application of small modular reactors (SMRs) in Kazakhstan. The meeting between the Chairman of the Atomic Energy Agency and the Deputy Assistant Secretary of State focused on the FIRST program, which assesses SMR technologies for Kazakhstan. Both sides expressed mutual interest in expanding cooperation in the peaceful use of atomic energy.

item.title: Trump reaffirms US support for Kazakhstan's independence and territorial integrity
item.description: Former US President Donald Trump sent a congratulatory message to Kazakhstan's President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev on Republic Day, noting the deepening partnership between the two countries. Trump reiterated Washington's unwavering support for Kazakhstan's sovereignty and territorial integrity, recalling that the US was the first to recognize Kazakhstan as an independent state in 1991. He described Kazakhstan's economic achievements as "remarkable."

item.title: Ukraine announces duration of Oleshki ceasefire initiated by Melania Trump
item.description: Ukraine has announced the duration of a temporary ceasefire in the Oleshki region, which began on November 27. The truce, initiated with the support of Melania Trump, aims to facilitate the evacuation of civilians and the delivery of humanitarian aid to the city.

item.title: Uzbekistan to Implement Advanced European Experience in Public Services
item.description: Uzbekistan is studying European best practices in public service delivery, focusing on reducing state involvement and enhancing market mechanisms. A delegation from the Ministry of Justice is examining models from Luxembourg and other EU countries to adapt them for Uzbekistan's system.

item.title: Man Sentenced to 16 Years for Drug Smuggling from Thailand into Kazakhstan
item.description: A 20-year-old foreigner has been sentenced to 16 years in prison for smuggling 17 kilograms of drugs from Thailand into Kazakhstan. The Ministry of Internal Affairs reported that since the beginning of the year, 98 kilograms of narcotics, valued at approximately 2.5 billion tenge, have been seized in Astana and Almaty airports.

item.title: UN Condemns Russian Missile and Drone Attacks on Kyiv; Ceasefire in Oleshky
item.description: Russia launched ballistic missiles and hundreds of drones at Kyiv, resulting in one death and at least 15 injuries. Attacks damaged university dormitories, residential buildings, and infrastructure. Ukrainian drones also attacked Russian territory. A local ceasefire is in effect in Russian-controlled Oleshky, Kherson region, for aid delivery and evacuation.

item.title: Kazakhstan proposed to establish a regional NVIDIA Physical AI Hub
item.description: Kazakhstan has proposed establishing a regional NVIDIA Physical AI Hub to train specialists and develop artificial intelligence solutions. This initiative was discussed during the visit of NVIDIA founder and CEO Jensen Huang. The first phase involves providing Kazakh universities access to NVIDIA DLI courses and certification for instructors. The goal is to leverage existing university infrastructure and cloud resources for AI education.

item.title: Masdar CEO: Uzbekistan creates favorable conditions for energy sector investors
item.description: Muhammad Jamil Al Ramahi, CEO of UAE's Masdar, stated that Uzbekistan offers all necessary conditions for investors in its energy sector. He noted that systemic reforms and strategic priorities are increasing foreign companies' interest and cooperation. The first Investor Council meeting in the fuel and energy sector, initiated by President Mirziyoyev, brought together international companies.

item.title: Finnish, Norwegian Leaders Discuss Ukraine War and Peace with Putin
item.description: Finnish President Alexander Stubb and Norwegian Prime Minister Jonas Gahr Store held a phone call with Russian President Vladimir Putin. The leaders initiated the discussion to address Russia's war in Ukraine and diplomatic efforts for peace. They conveyed Ukraine's position on upcoming peace talks in Abu Dhabi, aiming to strengthen European stability.

item.title: Ukraine's Oleshky Faces Russian Strikes as Ceasefire Agreement Takes Effect
item.description: A US-brokered ceasefire agreement for Oleshky, southern Ukraine, took effect on October 27, shortly after Russian airstrikes hit the city. The strikes damaged a university dormitory and other civilian buildings, killing at least one person. The ceasefire was intended to allow humanitarian aid delivery to the heavily affected city.

item.title: Kazakh Official Punished for Hindering Investor in Abai Region
item.description: A government official in Kazakhstan's Abai Region has been disciplined for obstructing an investor. The prosecutor's office intervened after discovering discrepancies in property registration for a sunflower oil processing plant in Semey. The delays prevented the investor from registering the facility and beginning operations. Following the prosecutor's action, the information system was updated, allowing the investor to proceed.

item.title: Kazakhstan to Consider Loans and Deposits When Assigning Social Assistance
item.description: Kazakhstan will now consider citizens' loans, deposits, and financial transactions when determining targeted social assistance. The Ministry of Labor and Social Protection stated that new criteria aim to ensure aid reaches truly needy families by evaluating their financial situation beyond just official income. This includes assessing bank loans, microcredits, outgoing bank transactions, and savings deposits.

item.title: Putin Supports Iran's Criticism of Western Unilateral Sanctions
item.description: Russian President Vladimir Putin has voiced support for Iran's criticism of Western unilateral sanctions, stating they negatively impact energy-producing nations and global energy supplies. Putin agreed with Tehran's stance, emphasizing that these sanctions affect not only producers but also consumer countries. The US and European nations have imposed sanctions on Russia and Iran targeting their energy exports.

item.title: Central Asians Losing Interest in Russian Citizenship Amid Shifting Perceptions
item.description: Over 4.7 million Central Asians obtained Russian citizenship in the 35 years since the USSR's collapse. Initially driven by higher salaries and simplified programs, interest has waned, especially after Russia's invasion of Ukraine. Experts cite the risk of conscription and societal discrimination as key deterrents.

item.title: Russian Cultural Center's History Lesson Sparks Controversy in Almaty School
item.description: A history lesson conducted by representatives of Russia's 'Rossotrudnichestvo' organization at School No. 32 in Almaty has drawn criticism. The event, focused on preserving historical memory and promoting a project, raised questions about the basis for a Russian state organization interpreting history within a Kazakh school.

item.title: Kazakhstan Announces Registration Dates for Master's and Doctoral Entrance Exams
item.description: Registration for Kazakhstan's comprehensive testing for master's programs and entrance exams for doctoral programs opens on October 28. The Ministry of Science and Higher Education confirmed the dates. Testing will take place in November and December, with applicants able to choose their testing city until November 10.

item.title: Tashkent Air Pollution: Scientists Identify Causes Amid Low Rainfall and Weak Winds
item.description: Scientists are investigating the reasons for increased dust in Tashkent's air, attributing it to rainfall being nearly six times below normal and weaker winds. Experts are conducting laboratory studies to identify pollution sources in the capital.

item.title: Kazakhstan Proposes Establishing Regional NVIDIA Physical AI Hub
item.description: Kazakhstan's Ministry of Science and Higher Education has partnered with NVIDIA on the Deep Learning Institute (DLI) program. Following NVIDIA CEO Jensen Huang's visit in October 2026, a proposal was made to establish a regional NVIDIA Physical AI Hub in Kazakhstan to foster talent and develop applied solutions in physical artificial intelligence.

item.title: Foreign National and Accomplice Sentenced for Organizing Illegal Entry into Kazakhstan
item.description: A foreign national residing in Kazakhstan and her accomplice have been sentenced for organizing illegal entry into the country. They charged 350,000 tenge for one illegal entry and attempted to smuggle another Uzbek citizen for $900. Both were found guilty of organizing illegal migration and received three-year sentences after amnesty.

item.title: Almaty Court Visits Construction Site Amid Housing Dispute
item.description: An Almaty court held an on-site hearing at the Premier residential complex construction site as part of a lawsuit filed by a construction company against journalist Vadim Boreiko. Residents shared concerns about problems arising from the construction, including lack of public hearings and alleged irregularities during excavation.

item.title: Clashes Erupt Between Taliban and Pakistani Forces on Paktika Border
item.description: Clashes have broken out between Taliban fighters and Pakistani forces in the Angoor Ada border area of Paktika province. Both sides reportedly used heavy weapons, leading to some residents fleeing their homes. The cause and casualties remain unconfirmed.

item.title: Turkistan Region Launches Projects Worth 60 Billion Tenge Ahead of Republic Day
item.description: In line with President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev's directives to improve infrastructure and create jobs, the Turkistan region has launched numerous projects valued at approximately 60 billion tenge. These initiatives span housing, healthcare, culture, sports, industry, and agriculture, with a focus on social infrastructure. The projects are expected to create 648 jobs.

item.title: Afghanistan Conducted Over 25,000 Anti-Drug Operations in 2026
item.description: Afghanistan's Ministry of Foreign Affairs reported that over 25,000 anti-drug operations were carried out in 2026. These operations resulted in the destruction of 26,500 hectares of poppy and cannabis crops and the arrest of 10,065 suspects. The announcement was made during a meeting in Kabul focused on the Islamic Emirate of Afghanistan's fight against drugs.

item.title: Kazakhstan and China Discuss Oil Supplies and Shymkent Refinery Expansion
item.description: Kazakhstan and China held their fifth working group meeting on oil and gas cooperation. Discussions included increasing oil supply volumes, expanding pipeline capacity, and developing petrochemical projects. Cooperation in subsoil use and new energy was also reviewed.
